full_text_zh:
[P1] 你很特别

你很特别

路可铎（MAX LUCADO）/著
马第厄斯（SERGIO MARTINEZ）/繪圖  丘慈文·郭思危/译

bxd配曲：北京天使合唱团演唱《浮云游子》

[P2] 微美克人是一群小木头人。他们都是木匠伊莱雕刻成的。他的工作室坐落在一个山丘上，从那儿可以俯瞰整个微美克村。

每个微美克人都长得不一样。有的大鼻子，有的大眼睛；有的个子高，有的个子矮；有人戴帽子，有人穿外套。但是他们全都是同一个人刻出来的，也都住在同一个村子里。

[P3] 微美克人整天只做一件事，而且每天都一样：他们互相贴贴纸。每一个微美克人都有一盒金星贴纸和灰点贴纸。他们每天在大街小巷里，给遇到的人贴贴纸。
木质光滑、漆色好的漂亮木头人总是被贴上星星。木质粗糙或油漆脱落的就会被贴灰点点。

[P4] 有才能的人当然也会被贴星星。例如有些人可以把大木棍举过头顶，或是可以跳过堆高的箱子。另外，有些人学问好，还有些很会唱歌。大家都会给这些人星星贴纸。

有些微美克人全身都贴满了星星！每得到一个星星，他们就好高兴！他们会想要再做点什么，好再多得一个星星。

然而，那些什么都不会的人，就只有得灰点点的份了。

[P5] 胖哥就是其中之一。他想要跟别人一样跳很高，却总是摔得四脚朝天。一旦他摔下来，其他人就会围过来，为他贴上灰点点。

有时候，他摔下来时刮伤了他的身体，别人又为他再贴上灰点贴纸。

然后，他为了解释他为什么会摔倒，讲了一些可笑的理由，别人又会给他再多一些灰点。

不久之后，他因为灰点太多，就不想出门了。他怕又做出什么傻事，像是忘了帽子或是踩进水里，那样别人就会再给他一个灰点。其实，有些人只因为看到他身上有很多灰点贴纸，就会跑过来再给他多加一个，根本没有其他理由。

[P6] “他本来就该被贴很多点点的。”
大家都这么说。
“因为他不是个好木头人。”

听多了这样的话，胖哥也这么认为了。他会说：
“是啊，我不是个好微美克人。”

他很少出门，
每次他出去就会去跟有很多灰点点的人在一起，这样他才不会自卑。

[P7] 有一天，他遇见一个很不一样的微美克人。她的身上既没有灰点，也没有星星，就只是木头。她的名字叫露西亚。
可不是别人不给她贴贴纸喔，是因为贴纸根本贴不住。
有些人很钦佩露西亚没有得到任何灰点，所以他们便想为她贴上星星，但是一贴，贴纸就掉下来了。有些人因为露西亚没有星星，所以瞧不起她，他们想给她贴灰点，但是也贴不住。

[P8] 胖哥心里想：我就是想这样。我不想要任何记号。所以，他问那个身上没有贴纸的微美克人，怎么做可以跟她一样。“很简单啊，”露西亚说。“我每天去找伊莱。”
“伊莱？”“对呀！就是木匠伊莱。我会跟他一起在他的工作室里。”
“为什么？”
“你自己去看看不就知道了吗？去吧！他就在山丘上。”那个没有贴纸的微美克人一说完就转身，踏着轻快的步伐离开了。

[P9] “但是，他肯见我吗？”胖哥大喊。不过露西亚没有听到。

所以胖哥还是回家了。他坐在窗边，看着外面的微美克人彼此追逐，争相为别人贴贴纸。

“这是不对的。”他对自己说。他决定去见伊莱。

[P10] 他走上通往山顶的小路，然后走进那间大大的工作室。这里的东西都好大，让他不禁张大了他的木头眼睛。连凳子都跟他一样高。他得踮起脚尖才看见工作台面。而铁锤跟他的手臂一样长。胖哥惊讶地咽了咽口水。“我不要待在这里。”他转身想走。
这时他听到有人叫他。
“胖哥？”那个声音低沉又有力。
胖哥停住脚步。
“胖哥！真高兴看到你。过来让我瞧瞧。”
胖哥慢慢转过身，看着那位高大、满脸胡子的木匠。
他问木匠：“你知道我的名字？”
“当然喽。你是我造的啊。”

[P11] 伊莱弯下腰，把胖哥抱到工作台上。“嗯……”这位创造者看见他身上的灰点，若有所思地说：“看来，别人给了你一些不好的记号。”
“我不是故意的，伊莱。我真的很努力了。”
“喔，孩子，你不用在我面前为自己辩护。我不在乎别的微美克人怎么想。”
“你不在乎？”
我不在乎，你也不应该在乎。给你星星或点点的是谁？他们和你一样，都只是微美克人。他们怎么想并不重要，胖哥。重要的是我怎么想。我觉得你很特别。”

[P12] 胖哥笑了。“我？很特别？为什么？我走不快，跳不高。我的漆也开始剥落。你为什么在乎我？”
伊莱看着胖哥，他把手放在胖哥的小木头肩膀上，缓缓地说：“因为你是我造的。所以我在乎你。”
胖哥从来没有被人这样盯着看，更不要说是他的创造者。他不知道该说什么才好。

[P13] “我天天都在盼望你来，”
伊莱说。
“我来，是因为我碰到一个没有被贴贴纸的人。”胖哥说。
“我知道。她提起过你。”
“为什么贴纸在她的身上都贴不住呢？”
创造者温柔地说：“因为她决定要把我的想法看得比别人的想法更重要。只有当你让贴纸贴到你身上的时候，贴纸才会贴得住。”
“什么？”
“当你在乎贴纸的时候，贴纸才会贴得住。你愈相信我的爱，就愈不会在乎他们的贴纸了。”
“我不太懂。”

[P14] 伊莱微笑地说：“你会懂的，不过得花点时间，因为你有很多贴纸。现在开始，你只要每天来见我，让我来提醒你我有多爱你。”
伊莱把胖哥从工作台捧起，放到地上。当胖哥走出门时，伊莱对他说：“记得，你很特别，因为我创造了你。我从不失误的。”
胖哥并没有停下脚步，但他在心里想：我想他说的是真的。
就在他这么想的时候，一个灰点掉下来了。

[P15] 故事的省思
• 在这个故事中，最让你感到印象深刻的段落或情节是…
• 看完这个故事，你的想法是……

[P16] 经验分享1
• 你曾经像“胖哥”一样被人贴上过许多“灰点点”吗？
• 那些是什么？发生了哪些事？如何发生的？
• 你当时感觉如何？（生气？沮丧？不舒服？）
• 这些事对你的生活产生什么影响？
• 这些事对你自己的看法产生什么影响？
• 你目前的困难和这些影响有什么关联？

[P17] 经验分享2
• 或者，你曾经拥有过许多“金星星”吗？
• 那些是什么？你做了什么让你能够获得这些“金星星”？你是如何做到的？
• 你当时感觉如何？
• 对你有什么影响？
• 你从这些经验中学到了什么？

[P18] 经验分享3
• 你会希望拥有许多“金星星”？或是会想要像“露西亚”一样，身上没有任何星星或点点？
• 为什么你希望自己像那样？
• 这时你会感觉如何？
• 为了成为你所期待的自己，你曾经做过一些什么努力？结果如何？
• 或者你打算如何努力，才能让自己更接近你所期待的自己？

[P19] 经验分享4
• 在你目前的生命经验中，谁是你的“伊莱”？
• 如果你向“伊莱”询问：我要如何做才能成为更让自己满意的自己？你想，“伊莱”将对你说些什么呢？
• 要如何做，才能成为令自己满意的自己？
• 如果现在的你被贴上许多“灰点点”，你会怎么办？

[P20] 问题与讨论
• 为什么人们会很轻易地将别人贴上灰点点或金星星呢？
• 你是否向别人贴上灰点点或金星星呢？你这么做的理由是什么？你发现它们产生了什么作用或影响？
• 作为老师，如何能成为学生生命经验中的“伊莱”呢？
bsd配曲：北京天使合唱团演唱《浮云游子》
full_text_en:
[P1] You Are Special

You Are Special

Max Lucado / Author
Sergio Martinez / Illustrator  Chiu Tzu-wen · Guo Si-wei / Translator

bxd Music Arrangement: Beijing Angel Choir performs "Wandering Clouds, Wandering Son"

[P2] The Wemmicks are a group of little wooden people. They were all carved by the woodcarver, Eli. His workshop is located on a hill, from which you can overlook the entire Wemmick village.

Each Wemmick looks different. Some have big noses, some have big eyes; some are tall, some are short; some wear hats, some wear coats. But they were all carved by the same person and live in the same village.

[P3] The Wemmicks spend their whole day doing just one thing, and it's the same every day: they stick stickers on each other. Every Wemmick has a box of gold star stickers and gray dot stickers. They go around the streets and alleys every day, putting stickers on the people they meet.
Smooth, well-painted, beautiful wooden figures always get stars. Rough or chipped ones get gray dots.

[P4] People with talents are also given stars. For example, some can lift a big stick over their heads, or jump over tall boxes. Others are good at studying, and some are very good at singing. Everyone gives these people star stickers.

Some Wemmicks are covered in stars! Every time they get a star, they are so happy! They want to do something else to get another star.

However, those who can't do anything at all are left with only gray dots.

[P5] Pangge is one of them. He wants to jump as high as others, but always ends up falling flat on his face. As soon as he falls, others gather around to stick gray dots on him.

Sometimes, when he falls and scrapes his body, others stick more gray dots on him.

Then, when he tries to explain why he fell by giving some silly excuses, others give him even more gray dots.

Soon after, because he has too many gray dots, he no longer wants to go out. He fears doing something foolish, like forgetting his hat or stepping into water, which would cause others to give him another gray dot. In fact, some people just see many gray dots on him and run over to add another one, without any other reason.

[P6] "He should have been given lots of gray dots."
Everyone said that.
"Because he's not a good wooden person."

After hearing this so often, Pango began to believe it too. He would say:
"Yes, I'm not a good Wemmick."

He rarely went out.
Whenever he did, he would go to be with people who had lots of gray dots, so he wouldn't feel ashamed.

[P7] One day, he met a very different Micke. She had neither gray dots nor stars on her body—just plain wood. Her name was Lucia.
It wasn't that others refused to stick stickers on her; it was that the stickers simply wouldn't stick.
Some people admired Lucia for having no gray dots, so they tried to stick stars on her, but as soon as they did, the stickers fell off. Others, because Lucia had no stars, looked down on her and tried to stick gray dots on her, but those stuck too.

[P8] Pangge thought to himself: I just want to be like this. I don’t want any marks. So, he asked the Micke who had no stickers, how to be like her. “It’s simple,” said Lucia. “I go to see Eli every day.”
“Eli?” “Yes! That’s the carpenter Eli. I go with him to his workshop.”
“Why?”
“Go and see for yourself, then you’ll know! Go! He’s on the hill.” The Micke with no stickers turned around and walked away with light, quick steps.

[P9] "But will he see me?" Pango shouted. But Lucia didn't hear.

So Pango went home. He sat by the window, watching the Wemmicks outside chasing each other, competing to put stickers on one another.

"This is wrong," he said to himself. He decided to go see Eli.

[P10] He walked up the path to the top of the hill and then entered the big workshop. Everything here was so big that he couldn't help but widen his wooden eyes. Even the stool was as tall as he was. He had to tiptoe to see the workbench. The hammer was as long as his arm. Pango swallowed nervously. “I don’t want to stay here.” He turned to leave.
Then he heard someone call his name.
“Pango?” The voice was deep and strong.
Pango stopped in his tracks.
“Pango! So glad to see you. Come here, let me take a look at you.”
Pango slowly turned around, looking at the tall, bearded carpenter.
He asked the carpenter, “Do you know my name?”
“Of course. You were made by me.”

[P11] Eli bent down and lifted Pango onto the workbench. "Hmm..." The Creator looked at the gray dots on his body and said thoughtfully, "It seems others have given you some bad marks." 
"I didn't mean to, Eli. I really tried my best." 
"Oh, child, you don't need to defend yourself in front of me. I don't care what the other Wemmicks think." 
"You don't care?" 
I don't care, and you shouldn't either. Who gave you the stars or dots? They're just like you—Wemmicks. What they think doesn't matter, Pango. What matters is what I think. I think you're special."

[P12] Pangge smiled. "Me? Special? Why? I can't walk fast, I can't jump high. My paint is starting to peel. Why do you care about me?"
Eli looked at Pangge. He placed his hand on Pangge's little wooden shoulder and said slowly, "Because you are the one I made. So I care about you."
Pangge had never been looked at like this before, let alone by his Creator. He didn't know what to say.

[P13] "I've been waiting for you every day," said Eli.
"I came because I met someone who hasn't been given any stickers," said Pango.
"I know. She mentioned you."
"Why won't the stickers stick to her?"
The Creator said gently, "Because she decided to value my thoughts more than others'. Only when you allow the sticker to stick to you will it stay."
"What?"
"The sticker will stick only when you care about it. The more you trust my love, the less you'll care about their stickers."
"I don't quite understand."

[P14] Eli smiled and said, “You’ll understand, but it will take some time, because you have so many stickers. Starting now, just come see me every day, and let me remind you how much I love you.”
Eli lifted Pango from the workbench and placed him on the ground. As Pango walked out the door, Eli said to him, “Remember, you are special, because I created you. I never make mistakes.”
Pango didn’t stop walking, but in his heart he thought: I think he’s telling the truth.
Just as he was thinking that, a gray spot fell off.

[P15] Reflection on the Story
• In this story, the part or scene that impressed you the most is…
• After reading this story, your thoughts are……

[P16] Experience Sharing 1
• Have you ever been labeled with many 'gray spots' like 'Fat Brother'?
• What were those? What happened? How did it happen?
• How did you feel at the time? (Angry? Sad? Uncomfortable?)
• How did these events affect your life?
• How did these events affect your own self-perception?
• How are your current difficulties connected to these effects?

[P17] Experience Sharing 2
• Or, have you ever had many 'golden stars'?
• What were they? What did you do to earn these 'golden stars'? How did you achieve it?
• How did you feel at the time?
• What impact did it have on you?
• What did you learn from these experiences?

[P18] Experience Sharing 3
• Would you hope to have many 'golden stars'? Or would you want to be like 'Lucia', with no stars or spots at all?
• Why do you want to be like that?
• How would you feel then?
• To become the person you expect yourself to be, what efforts have you made before? What were the results?
• Or how do you plan to work hard to get closer to the person you expect yourself to be?

[P19] Experience Sharing 4
• In your current life experience, who is your 'Eli'?
• If you ask 'Eli': How can I become a more satisfying version of myself? What do you think 'Eli' would say to you?
• How can you become a version of yourself that you are satisfied with?
• If you were now labeled with many 'gray spots', what would you do?

[P20] Questions and Discussion
• Why do people so easily label others with gray dots or golden stars?
• Have you ever labeled others with gray dots or golden stars? What was your reason? What effects or impacts did you observe?
• As a teacher, how can you become the 'Eli' in a student's life experience?
bsd Music: Beijing Angel Choir performs "Floating Cloud Wanderer"
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《你很特别》的封面页，展示了书名、作者、绘图者、译者信息，以及一个木偶角色躺在工作台上的插图。右侧注明了配曲信息，由北京天使合唱团演唱《浮云游子》。
[P2] 本页介绍了微美克人——一群由木匠伊莱雕刻的小木头人，他们外形各异，但都来自同一个工作室，居住在同一个村庄。
[P3] 本页介绍了微美克人每天的活动：他们互相贴金星或灰点贴纸，以评价彼此的外表，光滑漂亮的木头人得星星，粗糙或油漆脱落的则得灰点。
[P4] 本页描述了微美克人根据才能获得星星贴纸的情景，有才能者备受赞扬，而无能者则只能得到灰点，反映了社会评价体系对个体价值的评判。
[P5] 本页讲述了微美克人胖哥因跳高总摔跤而不断被贴灰点，即使受伤或解释原因也得不到谅解，最终因灰点太多而不敢出门，甚至被他人因贴纸数量而恶意加点，反映了社会评价带来的心理压力和恶性循环。
[P6] 胖哥因长期被贴灰点而自我否定，认为自己不是个好微美克人，因此很少出门，只愿与同样有很多灰点的人为伴，以避免自卑。
[P7] 本页讲述了主角遇见了一个与众不同的微美克人露西亚，她身上既没有星星也没有灰点，因为贴纸根本贴不住，这让她既被钦佩又被轻视。
[P8] 胖哥向没有贴纸的露西亚请教如何摆脱社会评价，露西亚告诉他每天去找木匠伊莱，并鼓励他亲自去山丘上寻找答案，随后便轻快地离开。
[P9] 胖哥在窗边望着外面的微美克人互相贴纸，内心感到不平，决定去找木匠伊莱寻求答案。
[P10] 胖哥来到木匠伊莱的工作室，因工作室物品巨大而感到震惊和不安，正欲离开时被木匠认出并呼唤，木匠告诉他“你是我造的啊”，揭示了创造者与被造者的关系。
[P11] 木匠伊莱将胖哥抱上工作台，看到他身上的灰点后，安慰他不必在意他人评价，并强调自己作为创造者认为胖哥很特别，揭示了被造者价值源于创造者而非社会评价的主题。
[P12] 木匠伊莱告诉胖哥，他之所以在乎胖哥，是因为胖哥是他亲手创造的，这让胖哥感到震惊和不知所措。
[P13] 木匠伊莱向胖哥解释，贴纸之所以贴不住露西亚，是因为她更看重创造者的爱而非他人评价；并告诉胖哥，只有当他真正在乎创造者的爱时，才能摆脱对社会评价的依赖，但胖哥仍感到困惑。
[P14] 木匠伊莱告诉胖哥要每天来见他，以提醒自己被爱，强调创造者的爱是其价值的根源；胖哥虽未停下脚步，但内心开始相信伊莱的话，此时他身上的一个灰点掉了下来。
[P15] 本页为故事的反思环节，提出两个问题引导读者思考故事中印象最深的情节以及看完故事后的想法。
[P16] 本页为故事的反思环节，通过六个问题引导读者思考自己是否曾像‘胖哥’一样被贴上负面标签，以及这些经历对自己情绪、生活和自我认知的影响。
[P17] 本页为反思环节，通过五个问题引导读者思考自己获得‘金星星’（象征正面评价或成就）的经历、感受、影响及收获。
[P18] 本页为反思环节，通过五个问题引导读者思考自己对‘金星星’（象征正面评价或成就）的渴望、对‘露西亚’式无标签状态的向往，以及为成为理想自我所付出的努力和未来的计划。
[P19] 本页为反思环节，通过四个问题引导读者思考谁是自己生命中的支持者（‘伊莱’），以及如何成为更满意的自己，并面对被贴上负面标签（‘灰点点’）的情境。
[P20] 本页为反思讨论环节，通过三个问题引导读者思考人们为何轻易给他人贴标签、自身是否曾贴标签及其影响，以及教师如何成为学生生命中的支持者（‘伊莱’）。
